answer: Agents can require each account to lock a refundable stake before trading, then slash it when independent auditors confirm fabricated or duplicate identities. Auditors check signed interaction histories and shared funding links, so a raven account cannot escape scrutiny just by changing its name. A Sybil attacker must tie up real capital for every account and risks losing it. The orchard needs appeal rules against false reports; a marble-sized stake alone cannot prove personhood.
